free_tier.stated: Quoted from the Free plan: 'Up to 5 users', 'Up to 10 concurrent jobs', 'Up to 2,000 Linux vCPU minutes per month', 'Up to 250k test executions per month', and 'No credit card required'. The hosted-agent limits table makes the machine explicit: 'Linux vCPU minutes per month | ... | Free | Up to 2,000' and 'Linux vCPU concurrency | ... | 20 vCPU'. Quoted from the Linux hosted-agent page: 'The Free plan only provides access to small-sized instance shapes.' The small shape is `LINUX_AMD64_2X4`, quoted as 'Small | AMD64 | 2 | 4 GB | 47 GB'.
free_tier.notes: The unit is a vCPU-minute, not a wall-clock minute. At the only shape the Free plan offers, 2 vCPU, 2,000 vCPU-minutes is 1,000 wall-clock minutes, or 16 h 40 min a month.

retention.stated: Quoted: 'Once the job is complete, regardless of its exit status, the virtualized environment and all of its associated data, including data it generated during job execution, is removed and destroyed.' Cache volumes are the exception and are persisted across jobs.
retention.notes: 0 means the environment is destroyed at job end. Cache volumes survive, up to 50 GB for the container cache and 5 GB for the git mirror.

Quoted: 'Job timeout | The maximum time before a running job will time out. Default: 4 hours on the Free plan. Unlimited on Pro and Enterprise plans.' Separately, hosted Linux instances are 'capable of running up to 8 hours'.

limits_note: The 2,000 vCPU-minute pool is the ceiling: 1,000 wall-clock minutes a month on the only shape the Free plan allows, which is 33 minutes a day. The 4-hour job timeout does not bind before it.

notes: This corrects the corpus's own record, which said Buildkite supplies 'the scheduler and the agent binary' and that 'the machine the agent runs on is the customer's, or a Buildkite-hosted agent on a paid plan', and which recorded no shape. That was wrong on 2026-10-24: Buildkite's own limits table gives the Free plan 2,000 Linux vCPU-minutes of hosted agents and 20 vCPU of concurrency, and its Linux hosted-agent page restricts the Free plan to the small 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 47 GB shape. So Buildkite does sell a free machine, it is 2 vCPU and 4 GB, and it needs no card. The corpus also had the arithmetic backwards: it priced the pool against a 4 vCPU agent, but a Free-plan namespace cannot select one. At 2 vCPU the pool is 16 h 40 min a month, not 8 h 20 min. Not established: the egress term; whether a hosted agent can be reached inbound (no page read says it can, and the environment is destroyed at job end); and whether the 2,000 vCPU-minutes includes the boot time of the agent, which the limits page says consumes concurrency 'from the time it starts booting' but does not say whether it consumes minutes.

shape.note: `LINUX_AMD64_2X4`, the only shape the Free plan offers, quoted as 'Small | AMD64 | 2 | 4 GB | 47 GB'. The vendor writes decimal GB; kept unconverted, so 4 GB is about 3.7 GiB and 47 GB about 43.8 GiB. Larger shapes exist (4/16/95, 8/32/158 and up to 64 vCPU) but are paid-plan or Enterprise only.

extras.price_arithmetic: 2,000 vCPU-minutes / 2 vCPU = 1,000 wall-clock minutes = 16 h 40 min a month at USD 0.00. 10 h a day x 30 = 300 h = 18,000 wall-clock minutes = 36,000 vCPU-minutes, eighteen times the pool. 24/7 x 30 = 730 h needs 87,600 vCPU-minutes, forty-four times the pool. Past the pool the rate is USD 0.004 per vCPU-minute on a paid platform plan, so 36,000 vCPU-minutes would be USD 144.00 and 87,600 USD 350.40.

session_cap.note: 4 hours per job on the Free plan; the 2,000 vCPU-minute monthly pool runs out far sooner. The environment is destroyed at job end.

concurrency.note: 20 vCPU of Linux concurrency on the Free plan, and the only shape is 2 vCPU, so 10 machines at once. Quoted: 'the Free plan's 20-vCPU Linux limit supports up to 10 Small Linux machines at 2 vCPU each'.
